text: Almost half the people who saw this ad clicked it.
It was the first banner ad on the web. October 1994.
say: It was the first banner ad on the web. October, nineteen ninety-four.

text: It ran on HotWired, the website of Wired magazine.
Their problem? The site was free to read. So how do you pay the writers?
Their answer: sell space on the page to advertisers, like a magazine does.
A spot reportedly cost $30,000 for 3 months.
say: A spot reportedly cost thirty thousand dollars for three months.

text: AT&T's ad just said: Have you ever clicked your mouse right here? You will.
say: A T and T's ad just said: Have you ever clicked your mouse right here? You will.

text: No product. No price. Nobody had seen an ad online before. About 44% clicked.
say: No product. No price. Nobody had seen an ad online before. About forty-four percent clicked.

text: Today, banner ads usually get clicked by well under 1 in 100 people.
say: Today, banner ads usually get clicked by well under one in a hundred people.

text: We trained our eyes to skip anything that looks like an ad. It's called banner blindness.
So if your website's key info sits in a flashy box, visitors may skip right past it.
